newsitem.title: FRANCE: France seeks to update state accounting methods.
newsitem.headline: France seeks to update state accounting methods.

text.p: The French government said on Wednesday it would present proposals in November to overhaul its accounting methods in order to give public decision makers a clearer picture of the state's finances.
The proposals -- part of France's drive to streamline government -- will be presented in the form of a "White Paper" and debated by Parliament.

The state "right now does not know how much its different services cost, it does not know how to compare results obtained with goals fixed," said a progress report presented by Finance Minister Jean Arthuis to the cabinet on Wednesday.

The White Paper will present various options and outline a five-year action plan aimed at allowing more efficient use of public resources by making accounting methods more transparent and precise, government spokesman Alain Lamassoure said.

Work on reforming the state's budget and accounting methods was begun in May 1996 by a group of experts headed by former defence minister Andre Giraud at the behest of conservative President Jacques Chirac.

The progress report presented by Arthuis highlighted certain areas where changes would be made. Those included estimating the value of real estate holdings, paying closer attention to performance of publicly held stakes and making the government's annual accounts clearer.
